content:
Hello!

We've all seen the new DTide Discourse. I wanted to throw my hat into the ring on how to make Madness difficulty better.

First, my understanding of the original reason Madness was added was so that the leaderboards wouldn't be full of people who got 425 with nowhere else to go; adding a mode which is hard enough that not everyone can clear it, so we don't have huge ties on the leaderboard, seems like a reasonable thing to do.

The problem is that huge HP pools are not a very interesting way to do it.

I would propose that instead of Madness as a separate difficulty per se, it could work as toggleable additions on to Nightmare:

If a nightmare wave gives 80 points, then we could have:
- -1 arithmetica: 1 point
- -3 arithmetica, superceeds above: 2 points
- -2 hand size: 1 point
- -6 hand size, superceeds above: 2 points
- -1 draw: 1 point
- +20 base alemus for all awakeners: 1 point
- +500 base keyflare cost: 1 point
- permanent weakness, vulnerability, void, etc: 1 point each
- Each awakener gets only one WoD: 3 points
- DR only works at >100%: 1 point
- etc

The specifics aren't super relevant/this is just a sketch and I would imagine BiAV would use different numbers, but I think the idea has some merit:
- Different teams will have different penalties which they find harder, allowing much more build diversity than the current Mega HP system
- If you have enough possible penalties, you'll end up with very very few (or no! Can't win with zero arithmetica) keepers with the top theoretical score, solving the original problem madness was set to fix
- If this goes well, you could use this same system for Madness/Nightmare story mode: Cap the level of story mode at 70/75/whatever it caps out for hard mode, and then have a "one star" nightmare victory need 3 bonus points, two stars 6, three stars 9, etc. 

And I think it would be easy to implement -- most/all of the effects already exist, so it could just be extra relics. 

I'd love to hear your thoughts!
thread_title: Suggestion For A Better Madness Mechanic

content:
I'm really gonna try my best to not be rude or contentious about this, but I am truly unhappy, and this news is ruining my enjoyment of the game just by knowing where we're headed. I seriously ask for you to reconsider, and give a proper explanation for why you're doing this.

The new alternate realms all hugely change how you use the realm mechanics, and by extension play the game in general. Regardless of if they're better or not, the common point between them is they're more restrictive to play, and offer far less control over how you use their mechanics. Personally, outside of PChaos, I don't find them fun. I much prefer the flexibility and ease of use of the normal realms, and I know I'm not alone in that opinion. Even if I do enjoy PChaos and want to see more of it, I still do not want it to become the new default given how huge of a departure it is from normal Chaos. To decide that these alt realms will be the new default going forward is a *massive* change to the core of the game, and you're making it far too gracelessly given the magnitude of it.

I understand that game design is difficult, and that some things truly are broken and require major fixes to work. So what is the problem with normal realms? What is this system and gameplay architecture that makes them unworkable now? What exactly is the vision for the future, and what point are you trying to achieve by doing this? Is there some kind of higher executive compelling you to do this and you simply have no choice? Please be honest.

And yes, I know about the JP server. I don't understand why we have to adopt their default. Why are they even a completely different game to begin with?

From my perspective, it seems like you guys are trying to brute force some vision that makes sense only to you, and not providing ample enough explanation for what you're doing or where we're headed.

I think you're treating this game as if it's still early in its life cycle and still trying to find its feet, where such massive changes would be more reasonable. But it's almost three years old and has a ton of working architecture and characters designed around it and a community that got used to it all. I wasn't around for when Faded Legacy became Astral Reign, though I hear that too was highly controversial. I understand 2.7 is going to be big; by any chance is there another massive ruleset change we'll be undergoing that once again reworks the whole game?

I know that the normal realms themselves took years of fine-tuning and tweaking to get right, and are you prepared to do that again with the new massively changed alt realms (PCaro especially)? Will old characters be redesigned to better fit in as well? That's a hell of a lot of new design debt you're taking on.

I think there is a fundamental misunderstanding about this situation.

Treating this as simply a “bugfix” overlooks an important point.

The Corposant + Horla Wheel interaction existed in the live game for over a year. It was never corrected or clearly communicated as unintended, so players naturally considered it part of Corposant’s actual performance.

The developers have testing environments and the ability to verify these interactions. If this was unintended, why was it left unchanged for over a year? And why were Corposant and Pickman rerun and sold without any warning that this interaction could later be removed?

Players invested based on the product and performance that were actually provided to them.

We are not asking the developers to keep a bug forever. We are asking them to recognize that removing a long-standing interaction after players have invested in it is, in practice, a nerf and a loss of investment value.

A reasonable solution would be to allow players to exchange Corposant and Pickman for selector tickets, so they can choose another character or wheel of equivalent value.

The issue isn’t that the bug was fixed.

The issue is that a long-standing part of Corposant’s actual performance was removed after players had already invested in her, including through a recent rerun.

We simply ask the developers to acknowledge the impact of this change and provide a reasonable solution.
